answer:
Your Lift note is now a full strength-training app. I could only preview it with sample data, so I haven't tapped through a real workout from start to finish. I did check the home, live-workout, history, progress and settings screens at phone and Mac widths. They load without errors, but I haven't exercised the buttons.

**What's in it**
- **Routines:**
  - Create, edit, duplicate and delete routines.
  - Move routines up and down, put them in folders, and reorder the folders.
  - Start a workout from a routine or empty.
  - Starting a second workout while one is running sends you back to the running one.
- **Live workout:**
  - Weight × reps with optional RPE, and warm-up, drop and failure set types.
  - The previous values show inline on each set. Tap them to copy them in.
  - A check completes a set. An automatic rest timer starts per exercise, with −15s, +15s and Skip, and it also shows on other screens. A duration clock runs the whole time.
  - Supersets, plus add, replace, reorder and remove exercises mid-workout.
  - Finishing shows a summary with duration, volume, sets and new PRs. You can save it as a routine.
- **Exercise library:** about 100 exercises with muscle group and equipment, search and filters, and custom exercises you can edit or delete. Each exercise has charts (best set, volume, estimated 1RM), a records tab (heaviest weight, est. 1RM, best set volume, best weight by reps) and its full history.
- **History:** a month calendar with workout days marked, a list of workouts, and a detail view. From the detail view you can repeat a workout, save it as a routine or delete it.
- **Progress:** this week's sets per muscle group, weekly volume and workouts-per-week charts, recent personal records, and a body-weight tab with an optional body-fat field.
- **Settings:** kg/lb, default rest, auto rest timer, RPE toggle, and a plate calculator with a bar weight and plates you own. There's also a button to restore the demo data or clear everything. The plate calculator is also available inside a live workout.
- **Demo data:** about 9 weeks of push/pull/legs training (Push A/B, Pull A/B, Legs A/B) with progressing weights and some missed sessions. It also includes 8 routines in two folders and body-weight entries.

The demo data is written into the app's data the first time you open the note, so `data.json` stays empty until then. Weights are stored in kg and converted to your unit for display.

The look is my own: an orange accent, with no Hevy branding, icons or media.
